value: local resource not guaranteed to map to unique global resource
note: The reported symptom is that the DXIL BACK END is what rejects this shader. This message is emitted only from `ResourceUseErrors::ReportError` in lib/HLSL/DxilCondenseResources.cpp (via dxilutil::kResourceMapErrorMsg, lib/DXIL/DxilUtilDbgInfoAndMisc.cpp:361), reached from LegalizeResourceUseHelper inside the DxilLowerCreateHandleForLib pass (`-hlsl-dxil-lower-handle-for-lib`, confirmed present in the ps_6_0 pipeline with `dxc -Odump`), which runs long after `-dxilgen`. Neither lib/Sema nor lib/SPIRV contains the string, so neither the front end nor the SPIR-V back end can produce it, and it cannot be satisfied by invocation 2 or 3 of the same capture. POSITIVE-ONLY, deliberately: (a) the capture holds three dxc invocations, so any absence clause would be answered for free by one of the other two; (b) a positive match here is already proof that Sema was silent, because a fatal front-end diagnostic stops compilation and the DXIL lowering passes would never run. NO source-location prefix is required and NO exit code is used: main prints `repro.hlsl:15:10: error: <msg>` while v1.4.1907 prints the same message locationless with `Use /Zi for source location.` appended, and dxc returns E_FAIL (0x80004005) for every ordinary diagnosed error, which is not an internal failure. The filename is not pinned, so a control run against a different shader can still fire this predicate. CAVEAT for anyone reading a no-match: it means only 'the DXIL back end did not emit this error'. That covers both the fix the issue asks for (Sema rejects it earlier) and a strictly worse outcome (nothing rejects it at all); match-sema.json is what separates them, and any no-match must be read by hand. CONTROLS: control-correct.hlsl -- the same shader with the resource assignment removed -- must NOT match (variant-correct-*.txt, --expect no-match); control-sema-mismatch.hlsl -- the same assignment with mismatched resource types, which Sema does diagnose -- must NOT match either, because Sema stops the compile before the back end runs (variant-sema-mismatch-*.txt, --expect no-match). repro-cs.hlsl, the compute restating published to Compiler Explorer, must MATCH (variant-cs-dxil-*.txt, --expect match), which is what licenses using it as a stand-in.
